subject: Transportation Systems
title: Dubai's Driverless Metro
description: A quick, practical guide to Dubai's Driverless Metro.

hook.text: Dubai's metro opened in 2009 as the world's longest fully automated driverless system.

buildup.text: Trains run on elevated tracks above the desert, controlled entirely by computers.

discovery.text: Gold Class carriages offer luxury seating, making public transit appealing even to car-loving residents.

twist.text: Dubai built it despite being a car city. The goal was to reduce traffic before it strangled growth.

climax.text: The system now carries over 200 million riders per year—proof that even car cities adopt metro.

punchline.text: Dubai proved that car cities can learn to ride trains.

quiz.question: What was notable about Dubai's metro when it opened?
options: The longest fully automated driverless system
